author: Rahul kp
title: Bank Reconciliation
hook: match your book with the bank!
simple_words: BRS explains why the Cash Book bank balance and the Pass Book balance are different.

definitions.meaning: A statement that reconciles the bank balance in the Cash Book with the balance in the Pass Book on a given date.
definitions.note: It is not a ledger account!

definitions.meaning: The bank's copy of the customer's account. A deposit is a credit in it, a withdrawal is a debit.

key_points: Differences arise from ==timing== (cheques not yet cleared) and from entries made by only one party.
Cheques issued but not presented, and cheques deposited but not yet credited, are timing differences.
Bank charges, interest and direct credits are known to the bank first; the Cash Book needs !!adjustment!!.
Timing items need no entry in books; errors and bank-only items need entries in the Cash Book.
formula_hook: start from Cash Book debit balance

rows: Bank charges, not in Cash Book
Direct credit by bank, not in Cash Book
Cheque dishonoured, not in Cash Book

insight.punchline: Flip the sign when you flip the start!
insight.text: Timing items affect only the Pass Book side; bank-only items affect only the Cash Book side.

memory_trick.explanation: Starting from the Cash Book balance: Issued-not-presented cheques are Added, Deposited-not-cleared cheques are Deducted. The Pass Book start reverses both.

steps: Note the starting balance and its Dr/Cr
Tick Cash Book against Pass Book
Apply the sign table to each item
Total gives the other book's balance
exam_tip: Read whether the question gives 'overdraft' or 'favourable' balance. An overdraft in the Cash Book reverses every sign.

doubt.question: Why is an overdraft shown as a credit in the Cash Book?
doubt.answer: Overdraft means the bank is owed money, so the Cash Book bank column has a credit balance. Pass Book shows it as a debit. All signs reverse.

mistakes.wrong: Passing journal entries for cheques issued but not presented
mistakes.right: No entry is needed. It is a timing difference and appears only in the BRS.

mistakes.wrong: Adding bank charges to the Cash Book balance
mistakes.right: Bank charges reduce the Cash Book balance, so deduct them.

mistakes.wrong: Using the same signs for an overdraft balance
mistakes.right: With an overdraft, every sign reverses. Check the balance type first.

mistakes.wrong: Treating a dishonoured cheque as a Pass Book error
mistakes.right: The bank has debited it. Deduct it in the Cash Book, since the Cash Book is not yet updated.
